open_requirements.requirement: taste gravity applies at every recommendation surface as a bounded influence layer after the blend, with a per-surface strength, reordering and never filtering
open_requirements.notes: PARTIAL 71adfa72 (first half): taste gravity is now a convex mixture served=(1-g)*base+g*taste, both terms normalised to 0..=1 over the page; unbounded multiplier replaced. Reorders never filters (same length/elements asserted); the algorithm's own score is NOT rewritten; stable ties; egalitarian mode still switches it off. Per-surface strength via [taste] gravity_per_surface + gravity_ceiling (refused outside 0..=1 at load, and it bounds the number in force including the global value) + gravity_locked; TasteConfig::strength_for(surface). The feed publishes gravity{mode,strength,moved_up,moved_down,unchanged} - mode and a coarse pull, never a score or per-item reason. NOT DONE: story.similar / library.because_you_shelved and the other registry surfaces have no candidate pipeline to pull on, so discover.feed and the concierge (`home.curated`) honour the layer (1f05deff); taste_signal SHIPPED f74bd400: darkhold_db::taste_signal::for_account scores each candidate by the share of ITS canonical entities that appear on the works the account has shelved (share of the candidate, not of the shelf); absent from the map = unmeasured, Some(0.0) = measured and cold, None = no shelf at all; wired on both gravity surfaces. Ratings would be a better input and are not stored per reader (work_ratings holds an aggregate mu/phi/sigma), which is named in the module. END-TO-END f52beefd: a shelved reader's feed ranks the work sharing the shelf's tag above one sharing nothing at pull 1.0 (mutation: inverted affinity reddens it), and the published pull is now measured at the END of the pipeline (PullHistogram::between) because M45's taste ordering moves rows after gravity and the mid-pipeline histogram said 'nothing moved' on a page whose order had changed. Still missing: the surfaces without a candidate pipeline (story.similar, library.because_you_shelved). the reader's dial SHIPPED c9e4527d: migration 0171 reader_gravity + GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/discovery/gravity, narrowing only (refused above the instance, out-of-range refused not clamped, locked refuses with the lock named, DELETE clears rather than storing 0.0, stored values clamped on read), and the feed applies it; the gravity block reports strength (in force) beside instance. Original note: P9. served = (1-g)*algorithm + g*taste_match, taste_match from the operator profile (§16.2) over fandom/tag/author/source. Default g = 0.15; story.more_by_author = 0.0, story.similar = 0.10, home.trending = 0.35. Constraints: reorders never filters (M43-02), floor/ceiling are configuration (§16.16's shape), the reader's dial reaches zero unless locked (§16.5), no per-item reason is printed and no score is exposed (§0.3) while the mode and a coarse pull histogram are published, and gravity is measured as its own experimental arm so 'it helped' is a number.

open_requirements.requirement: co_shelving: reading lists are first-class (create, curate, publish, follow) and list co-occurrence feeds story.similar and library.because_you_shelved
open_requirements.notes: P11, the endgame signal and the one with the longest lead time: it needs lists to exist and to be used before it has any rows. Design lists first so the data accumulates from the day the feature ships. PARTIAL ee413789: co_shelving is an engine (db::discovery::co_shelving_recommendations) reading PUBLIC shelves only - readers who shelved what you shelved; own shelved works excluded; published/public targets only; engine_reason now maps co_shelving and the slot reason is ReadingHistory. Lists already create/curate/publish (library.rs shelves + is_public). FOLLOWING A LIST SHIPPED e62ab963: migration 0172_shelf_follows, db::shelf_follows (follow/unfollow/followed_shelves/follows), GET /shelves/following + POST|DELETE /shelves/{id}/follow; unpublished and own shelves refused 422, invisible shelf 404, follow idempotent, a shelf made private disappears from followers' lists while the row survives (mutated is_public predicate reddens). NOT DONE: story.similar / library.because_you_shelved / story.lists_containing have no candidate pipeline, so the engine is reachable from the discover feed only.

open_requirements.requirement: co_read: session transitions feed story.also_enjoyed, with bot and single-click traffic excluded
open_requirements.notes: P12. Needs M64-02's logging. Noisy by nature; the threshold is a minimum transitions-per-item before an edge is usable.

open_requirements.requirement: engagement_overlap at reader-cluster level with k-anonymity (a minimum number of readers per cluster) and aggregation thresholds, exposing no per-reader signal
open_requirements.notes: P13. Feeds author.similar, library.fill_the_gap and story.similar. The privacy floor is the gate: below the threshold the algorithm reports unmeasured rather than pretending.

open_requirements.requirement: embedding similarity for summaries first and full text last, feature-gated on a configured AI provider and degrading to disabled rather than erroring
open_requirements.notes: P14. The spec already names embedding and matrix-factorisation strategies as provider-gated (§16). Summary embeddings are the cheap half; full-text style matching needs the bodies, which the catalogue deliberately does not store.

open_requirements.requirement: the operator console lists every live experiment per surface with its numbers, allows hold, promote and preview-as-persona, and shows why each promotion happened
open_requirements.notes: P15. Promotion is automatic (M64-04); this is the surface where the operator can disagree without editing a table. preview-as-persona reuses M45-46 (preview before apply). PARTIAL 7e58e239: GET /api/v1/operator/experiments (operator-only, 404 for a reader) lists every surface with numbers per arm (impressions, readers, guest_readers, events, conversion_rate), the override the feed is running, and the last decision verbatim (day, lift, evidence, algorithms_before/after) - passed through rather than recomputed, so the console cannot disagree with the record. Tested behaviourally (operator sees impressions 1000 / rate 0.1; reader gets 404 on both operator doors). WRITE HALF 0612cdf7: migration 0170 experiment_holds + experiment_decisions.source (automatic|manual); POST/DELETE /operator/experiments/{surface}/hold (a held surface is skipped by the sweep and REPORTED as held, reason required), POST .../promote {algorithms} and .../demote, both through record_manual which writes the same row shape and installs/clears the override identically, distinguished only by source. NOT DONE: preview-as-persona (needs a reader-shaped view for a chosen pseud - a different mechanism from a write).

open_requirements.requirement: guest access with consent: a reader may read before registering, and the consent gate exists before the surface it gates. The estate standard sets the free-to-read boundary; this site's only delta is guest.mau_limit = 500.
open_requirements.notes: Adopted from the estate standard (secondbrain 2026-10-16-guest-access-trust-and-self-governance.md). Config delta for this site: guest.mau_limit = 500. Blocked on GS-3 (the guest identity is a cookie, so the consent gate must exist before the thing it gates).

open_requirements.requirement: the guest fold moves reading progress and bookmarks with the guest: progress and bookmarks are the guest's most valuable and most private artifact, so registering moves them rather than abandoning them, and nothing is published about a guest beforehand.
open_requirements.notes: Firewall specific to this site: reader-visible data is the guest's most valuable and most private artifact, and nothing may be published about a guest before they register. Ordered after GS-3 because offering guest access without the fold creates work to clean up later.

open_requirements.requirement: guest identity as a first-class pseudonym: the guest identity is a cookie-backed pseudonym that upgrades in place on registration, and it comes first because the gate has to exist before the thing it gates.
open_requirements.notes: Measured 2026-11-02: consent appears only in crates/app/tests/milestone_16.rs; no guest identity and no fold exist in this tree. The standard names this first because the gate has to exist before the thing it gates.

open_requirements.requirement: elastic trust from karma, not a parallel score: trust is derived from the karma terms already in this tree (karma: 99 references, trust_level: 52) rather than a parallel score, because two trust numbers that disagree is the failure mode.
open_requirements.notes: An upgrade of machinery that exists rather than new machinery: karma (99 references) and trust_level (52) are already here. Two trust numbers that disagree is the failure mode. Cheap to fake, so it needs a test that would pass for the wrong reason, written and killed on purpose.

open_requirements.requirement: a jury drawn from the eligible pool: governance decisions are made by a jury drawn from the eligible pool; cheap to fake, so it needs a test that would pass for the wrong reason, written and killed on purpose.
open_requirements.notes: The other item nothing in this repo has. Same caution as GS-4: the numbers belong in the roadmap file when they are real.

open_requirements.requirement: P2P local file sharing over the LAN and by direct link, with a seeding network later: a reader serves their own files to another person directly — no relay, no DHT, no node discovery, no global namespace — and their files stay their own files.
open_requirements.notes: The first milestone is deliberately smaller and shippable: serve local files to another person on the LAN or by a direct link, with no relay, no DHT, no node discovery and no global namespace; the user's own files stay their own files. Items 50, 51, 61, 69 and 96 belong to it (drag-drop import, local full-text search, offline queue, Calibre metadata.db ingestion, a local engine over local edges). The seeding network (81, 93, 98, 99) is a later spec that needs a threat model first — a document, not a weekend.

open_requirements.requirement: peering is suggested by cosine similarity over that fingerprint, and a colliding hardcoded filter blocks it outright
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §16.2. Two thresholds and one veto: similar enough to suggest, unrelated enough to ignore, and a hardcoded-filter collision is a block, not a warning. The veto is the half that matters for darkhold, whose hardcoded layer is illegal content rather than taste: two instances that disagree about that layer must not peer at all. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: a signed taste passport moves a reader's taste and contribution history between instances, suki and darkhold alike
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §16.3. A reader leaving for a peer takes a signed document — taste vector, favourite source URLs, edit counts, affinity at origin. darkhold already recomputes from behaviour (M11-01/M11-03), so the passport bootstraps rather than replaces: it answers where a reader starts without starting at zero. ed25519 over canonical JSON, and a receiving instance treats it as a claim, never as a fact. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: a takedown is a tombstone that survives re-import, and the importer refuses the work citing the original
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §5.5 and §13.2 step 3. darkhold has DMCA intake planned (M45-52) and nothing that stops the same work returning through the pawchive importer the next day, which is the failure a takedown exists to prevent. Keyed by work identity rather than URL: a re-import from another host is the same work. Synergy: suki syncs tombstones across peers; a tombstone that only stops the local importer is half a takedown. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: mirroring by taste similarity, with the mirror visible as attribution on the work page rather than as a silent copy
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §16.4 ('preserved by'). M45-39 covers instance-death protection as paperwork (mutual backup, dead-man's switch); this is the reader-visible half. Attribution is not decoration: without it a mirror looks like plagiarism, and the author's page is the second place a reader looks. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: a perceptual-hash rescue ring: after a peer dies, a work's media is recovered by hash match from survivors
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §16.4. darkhold already computes perceptual hashes for media (M32-07a/07b), so the join exists: (pHash, dimensions, duration) against a surviving peer. Recovery is proposed, never automatic — a hash collision that silently attaches the wrong image to a work is worse than a missing image. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: an evacuation protocol: an instance announcing shutdown exports to taste-similar peers, and says who took what
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §16.4. M45-39 has the switch; this has the recipient list and the receipt. The receipt matters when two peers both claim the same work — the author's page must not fork. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: affinity is a stored 0..1 score per reader, recomputed nightly, not a per-work multiplier
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §3.3. darkhold stores operator affinity per WORK (M11-03) and a resonance score (M45-51); neither answers how close a reader is to the operator, which is what gates trust speed, badges and membership. Nightly recomputation from favourite overlap, tag co-occurrence and arena agreement keeps it out of the request path. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: the arena ranks by Glicko-2 — deviation, volatility, a divergence flag — rather than Elo at K=32
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §10.2. darkhold's arena is Elo (M45-02) and the community board would inherit it (M44-02 planned). Elo has no notion of confidence: a work with two votes and one with two hundred sit on the same ladder. Glicko-2 yields rating, RD and volatility, which is what makes 'provisional' honest and lets pairing prefer uncertain pairs. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: arena pairing prefers similar ratings with high deviation, explores occasionally, and calibrates new works without moving the global rank
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §10.3 and §10.4. Proximate pairing plus epsilon-greedy exploration, and a first-N-votes calibration window recorded but not applied to the global ladder. Without the calibration window a new work inherits its first voter's taste as a fact. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: trust velocity: progression multiplied by taste alignment and behaviour quality, clamped, and never a demotion
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §4.2. darkhold has trust levels (M14-01) and a spam-report demotion (DM3-06), but progression is flat: every account earns at the same rate for the same acts. Clamped to [0.25, 2.5], and the row is explicit that it can slow a reader and can never take a level away — the demotion path is the report, not the multiplier. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: a live badge, gained and lost as taste drifts, unlike the episodic awards that already exist
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §3.4 (Attuned). darkhold's badges are one-time facts (M47-14 'First Words'), and a one-time badge cannot express a relationship that changes. Recomputed with affinity, and a lost badge emits its own event, because a badge that vanishes silently reads as a bug. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: taste-gated membership: above a configured population, new readers get a probation and the floor rises with the instance
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §4.3. The row with the most ways to be cruel, so it is written with its exits: probation is time-bounded, the floor is configurable, existing readers are grandfathered, and a reader who does not graduate is redirected with a passport rather than deleted. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: content filtering in three layers — hardcoded, policy, taste — with overrides that carry a reason and an audit trail
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §11.1 and §11.2. darkhold has per-reader content filters and reader-warning preferences but no layer model, so every filter is equally overridable and the one that must not be sits in the same list as the ones that may. A policy override is allowed and warns; the hardcoded layer has no override path at all. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: a tag assertion records who asserted it — human, source, model, community — and a model may only propose
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §6.3 and §6.4. darkhold's resolution hierarchy carries provenance for VALUES (M47-01) but a tag link does not say whether a person or an importer put it there, which is what decides whether it may be silently corrected. The write order is the invariant: provenance is set before anything can overwrite it. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: trope clusters with a coverage checklist, so a work knows which trope families it never names
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §6.5. darkhold has tag families and a canonical taxonomy but no notion of coverage — the closest thing is a tag count, which says nothing about what is missing. Clusters are operator-editable and priority-ordered, and the checklist is advisory: a work is not incomplete for lacking a trope, it simply knows it has none. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: a tag script: a persistent set of assertions applied to works while browsing, so gardening is a mode rather than a form
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §15.2. darkhold has batch operations (M53-01) and a single-work editor; neither makes repeated judgement cheap. The script is visible in the header whenever it is armed, because a mode that silently rewrites tags is how people stop trusting a site. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: Saved Filters: one saved view — filter, sort and blend — with a slug, subscriptions, keybind and a pinned feed
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §8.2–§8.5, renamed on 2026-11-02. The mechanism already exists in this archive's own vocabulary: a saved view (§14.2 'Saved searches and named views'), a versioned JSON AST (M8) rendered by the query language (M10-04, implemented), pinnable to the sidebar with its own sort, and already able to produce an RSS feed. What this row adds is the object's public life: a slug URL, sharing, subscribing, a number-key binding, and a pinned blend — not a second query engine, and not a second storage shape. Naming, decided and written into §14.2: the reader-facing term is **Saved Filter**, and the stream it produces is a **feed**; "lens" is retired (booru jargon from a sibling project) and "recipe" stays reserved for the ephemeral per-session condition. `extends M63-06` (the terminal's save) and `M63-09` (the query library on disk) supply the two non-web doors. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: the morning queue and the daily surprise, expressed as Saved Filters over surfaces that already exist
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §14.6, renamed 2026-11-02 (was 'lenses'). darkhold has a Blind Date (M66-04) and hidden classics (M66-05); the morning queue is the missing half — a small, bounded, deliberately diverse set rather than one pick. Written as a Saved Filter, not a surface, so the operator can retune it without a deploy, and so a reader can see the filter behind what they were shown. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: an import source can carry a Saved Filter as intake policy: what this source may bring in, and what it queues
open_requirements.notes: Suki spec §8.4 (import filter) and §11.4, renamed 2026-11-02 (was 'lens'). darkhold's importers decide by host and by rule (M67-03/04); a Saved Filter makes the policy a shareable object the operator can test by running it, which is the difference between a policy an operator can inspect and one they have to trust. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: one shared taste crate and one JSON schema set, so darkhold and suki compute blend, affinity and the passport identically
open_requirements.notes: The synergy row, and the one that keeps the others honest: two products that each implement the blend will disagree within a month, and a passport whose semantics differ between sender and receiver is worse than none. A small Rust crate with no product dependencies plus versioned JSON schemas; both binaries depend on it, neither forks it. Default off: it changes what a stranger sees or what the instance claims about itself, so it waits for a decision rather than a default.

open_requirements.requirement: both identity gates see the spellings the schema actually uses: bare `account`, `created_by`, `pseud_id`
open_requirements.notes: Measured 2026-11-02 while closing M45-62, from the migrations rather than from memory: 68 identity-carrying columns sit outside the foreign-key graph, and neither gate can see 37 of them. `scripts/check-snapshot-pii.py`'s IDENTITY_NAME_RE matches account_id, user_id, owner_id, author_id, actor_id, e-mail/password, token/secret/api_key, ip, user_agent, real name, phone, address, lat/long, device_token, endpoint, session_id, cookie, fingerprint — and not a bare `account`, not `created_by`, not `pseud_id`. `crates/db/tests/erasure_covers_fk_free_accounts.rs` matches account_id, *_account and *_account_id — and not a bare `account` or `created_by`. So 25 bare `account` columns (taste_profiles, dashboard_layouts, group_members, conversation_participants, presence, wishlists, event_participation, trust_levels, sanctions, operator_role, credit_entries, credit_holds, subscriptions, usage_counters, extension_grants, push_subscriptions, ai_requests, privacy_requests, reader_work_progress, forum_throttle_log, exchange_terms, ...) and 12 `created_by` columns (challenges, events, bounties, translation_jobs, announcements, directory_lists, categories, category_proposals, entry_moderation_proposals, taxonomy_edges, ...) are decided by nothing but habit. The fix is not "add a regex alternative": both gates compare measured against classified in BOTH directions, so widening the pattern turns them red until all 68 columns carry a treatment, and each treatment is a judgement (pseud vs account vs public handle) that has to be read off the writer — RequirePseud or RequireSession in the handler that inserts the row. That inventory IS the ticket; the regex is one line of it. Second finding, fixed already and worth keeping: the snapshot gate was not in CI at all, so it had been red in a clean tree since M47-14 with nothing to notice. It runs now (.github/workflows/ci.yml).

open_requirements.requirement: 29 community roadmap feature consensus: readers propose what the platform builds next, the community ranks the proposals against each other, and an operator moves cards across a board
open_requirements.notes: Reserved section, specified in docs/spec/29-community-roadmap-feature-consensus-and.md. Registered 2026-11-02 while making the ideas generator able to run at all (M65-08): its coverage gate had been refusing because this idea had no home.

open_requirements.requirement: 44 roadmap consensus an elo ranked community voted board: a public board where the community ranks feature ideas by pairwise consensus, ported from FicHub's fichub-consensus Elo design
open_requirements.notes: Reserved section, specified in docs/spec/44-roadmap-consensus-an-elo-ranked-community-voted.md. Registered 2026-11-02 for the same reason as M29-08: an idea the coverage gate named with no home.

open_requirements.requirement: §21.4's execution sandbox: `wasmi` with fuel, memory ceilings, output limits, host-call limits, bounded concurrency, hard wall-clock termination, host-I/O timeouts, and revocation that stops a running package.
open_requirements.notes: NOT BUILT and deliberately so: there is no `wasmi` dependency in the workspace. Trust and subscription tiers change resource ceilings, never permissions — that distinction is already encoded in the manifest, so the sandbox has something to enforce that is not its own policy. The path is specified and gated by M45-57 for source adapters; building the executor is the prerequisite for M16-07, M16-08 and M16-12.

open_requirements.requirement: §21.5's review workflow: submitted → automated checks → permission review → security review → independent quorum approval → published, with renewed consent when permissions grow, and emergency revocation with rollback.
open_requirements.notes: The storage exists (`extension_submissions`, `extension_manifests`, `extension_grants` in 0018_marketplace.sql) but the workflow itself is not built: no quorum, no renewal-of-consent path, no rollback. Free and paid extensions follow the same review — a paid status that skipped security review would be a way to buy the review.

open_requirements.requirement: §21.6's gallery mechanics: idempotent installation, one active installation per package and pseud scope, version pinning and update policy, uninstall, ratings and written reviews, install counts with documented semantics, remix/fork lineage with attribution preserved, and licence compatibility checks.
open_requirements.notes: NOT BUILT as a gallery. M70-10 builds the document-browse subset deliberately without ratings or install counts: on a corpus of four, ranking by popularity makes the first uploader permanently first. Forking must not bypass review or copy grants; install counts must not be inflatable by reinstalls, and individual installation histories are never public.

open_requirements.requirement: §21.9's paid marketplace, separate from credits: purchases, entitlements, refunds, developer revenue accounting, optional processor-backed payouts, the 85/15 reference split, and operator tax/invoicing setup.
open_requirements.notes: NOT BUILT. Credits are the closed-loop economy (M45-18) and this is deliberately a separate ledger; mixing them would let a credit balance become a price. No processor integration exists, so the 85/15 split is a number in a spec with nothing to divide.

open_requirements.requirement: §21's acceptance list: infinite loops terminate, memory excess fails safely, host APIs enforce permission denial, revoked packages stop running, uninstall removes grants, reset remains reachable after a broken theme, forks keep attribution and request their own grants, and custom engines and recipes honour opt-out.
open_requirements.notes: NOT MET — every item except 'reset remains reachable' (there is no theme to break) and 'opt-out honoured' needs the executor from M16-06. Written as one row because these are the claims that make the rest of §21 trustworthy, and splitting them would let the easy half be declared done.

open_requirements.requirement: §21.7's theme model beyond one stylesheet: design tokens, constrained layout slots, scoped styling, preview, reset, safe mode, accessibility checks — and the rule that a theme cannot hide the positivity filter status, the feedback mechanism, the safety controls or the extension management interface.
open_requirements.notes: NOT BUILT. M70-06 gives a reader a stylesheet; this is the model underneath that makes a theme composable, previewable and undoable. The cannot-hide rule is the one that needs a mechanism rather than a rule: a theme is CSS, and CSS can hide anything, so the safety surfaces have to live outside the document a theme styles — either in a shadow root, an iframe, or a separately-styled region the theme cannot select.

open_requirements.requirement: §21.8's operational half: rotating secrets, a per-subscription rate limit, and auto-disable of a subscription that keeps failing.
open_requirements.notes: NOT BUILT. Delivery retries and records, but nothing rotates a secret, nothing limits a subscriber's request rate, and a permanently failing endpoint keeps being tried — which is both a resource leak and a way to keep probing an endpoint that has moved.

open_requirements.requirement: Every db listing query that a reader surface depends on is either wired to a route or deleted: no function exists only to satisfy its own test.
open_requirements.notes: Found while implementing M70-12 and confirming it with a live probe. `content::list_public_works_by_freshness` is called by nothing in crates/app — its only callers are crates/app/tests/publication_events.rs and the M70-12 test — so the ordering guarantees it asserts (event-log `new` vs `updated`, NULL publish events sorting last) are proven about a function no reader can reach. Two honest ends: wire it into the home/freshness feed (and check whether the feed that exists today reproduces those guarantees), or delete it and move the ordering assertions onto the SQL that does serve. The probe that surfaced it: /api/v1/works?sort=new is the AUTHOR's list and answers AUTH_REQUIRED to a stranger, and the stranger's feed comes from browse.rs, not from this function. RATCHET 2026-11-06 (f19ecf18): crates/app/tests/orphan_queries.rs fails when a NEW db function is reachable only from tests; baseline in docs/plans/orphan-queries.txt, generated by scripts/orphan-queries.py (294 orphans measured today); a second test fails when the list names a function that no longer exists. ROW STAYS PLANNED: the requirement is every listing query wired or deleted, and 294 are neither. The named case in this row (content::list_public_works_by_freshness) IS wired - the landing page reads it (8a51f9de). Next step for the row: work the baseline down crate by crate, starting with the archives/import surfaces where a wired route is the honest end and a deletion would lose an operator capability.

open_requirements.requirement: Browse, search, library and the overflow view of every recommendation rail render results as dense list rows — title, author, provenance word, word count, unit count, completion, rating, date, metrics — with a stated total and cursor pagination, never a card grid and never infinite scroll.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 2, no new backend. 141,317 catalogue rows behind a card grid is the strongest finding in the external design and the cheapest. Sorts stay the closed vocabulary; sort changes order and never hides results (§8.1). Row height consistent; quick actions on hover/focus, always visible on mobile.

open_requirements.requirement: The operator console becomes its own visual register: dense rows, monospace values, red/amber/green status with a word, an alert bar naming every red state with a 'fix' link, 404 for non-operators, and no component shared with the reader-facing site that would soften a failure.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 3. §8.20 made operational: the console is allowed to be less beautiful than the reader and is not allowed to hide a red state. Today the ~30 admin surfaces use the same component library as the reading site. Acceptance: the admin overview renders each group from live counts and every warning has an action; a non-operator gets 404.

open_requirements.requirement: The reader gains an auto-hiding bar (back, unit navigation, position, typography, bookmark, in-work search) and a typography panel whose settings are per reader and per work, with provenance shown ('your default' / 'instance default' / 'this work') and a reset at each level.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 2, additive to the existing server-rendered reader. Typography must stay independent of the site theme (§4.11 of the proposal); the panel offers font family including a dyslexia-friendly option, size, line height, measure in characters, justification and four functional presets. Acceptance: settings survive a device change; an RTL work and an LTR work do not share them; the panel renders without JS as a form.

open_requirements.requirement: Reader position is honest: a position recorded against an older revision is reported as stale and offered as a choice, two devices that disagree are offered as a choice, and a position with no reliable evidence renders '—' rather than a false 0%.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 3. The anchor system exists; the honesty layer does not. §8.14 and §8.17 make silence and silent overwrite both bugs; §11 forbids fake precision. Acceptance: three tests, one per state, each asserting the choice text and that no percentage is fabricated.

open_requirements.requirement: Facet counts are a server capability with a latency budget: one endpoint returns counts per facet value under the current filter set, the UI renders them per group and shows '—' while they update, and the p95 stays inside the budget on the 141k-row catalogue.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 3, and the most underpriced item in the external design: no route in the 720 returns a facet count (grep '"facets"' crates/app/src is empty). This is an aggregate query plan — indexes, a cache, a budget — not a component. Acceptance: a load measurement with the decision rule fixed before the run, documented in the row.

open_requirements.requirement: The word-count filter is a real histogram: a distribution endpoint returns ten buckets for the current filter set, the control draws them and lets a range be selected over the bars, and the selected bounds are stated as numbers.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 4, depends on M71-11's aggregate surface — same query shape, different grouping. Decorative bars fed by invented data are forbidden (the proposal is right that the histogram must be real).

open_requirements.requirement: Every surface that enumerates a partially covered dimension states its coverage: the fandom facet leads with 'N of M works are tagged (P%)', fandom and source pages split hosted from referenced, and the numbers come from one aggregate view rather than being typed into copy.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 3. 5.4% fandom coverage is a fact the CLI already prints and the UI hides; a catalogue that hides it is claiming a completeness it does not have. Acceptance: the numbers on a page equal a query's output, asserted in a test.

open_requirements.requirement: Settings show inheritance with provenance at every level (instance, account, pseud, per-work), deep-link to the exact control, offer a reset at each level that overrides, and reflect inline changes made elsewhere with a 'set as default' affordance.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 4. The product already has per-work reader overrides and content filters enforced server-side; the settings surface does not explain where a value came from, so an override looks like a bug. Locked chips for server-enforced filters carry a link to settings and no dismiss control (§8.16).

open_requirements.requirement: The query string and the facet panel are one state: every facet is expressible in the grammar, or it is rendered as a visible chip that cannot be dropped by editing the string — no filter may disappear because it had no field.
open_requirements.notes: Priority 3. The query grammar has no fields for provenance, source or language; a design that presents the string as the state would silently drop those filters, which is hidden state the product forbids (§8.2 closed vocabulary, §8.14 named degradation).

open_requirements.requirement: The remaining document-class pages migrate in ADR 0006's order - work page /works/{id}, fandom and tag pages, search results, author and collection/series pages - each shipped as server-rendered HTML whose content, links and primary action work with no script, with its Svelte route deleted in the same commit and a server test asserting the no-JS content.
open_requirements.notes: Opened by M71-01 (8a51f9de), which shipped the landing page. Order and reasons are in docs/adr/0006-one-binary-two-renderers.md. The work page is next and is the one that matters for link previews and crawlers: it needs the public view (works::public_view) plus a session-aware split, because the SPA work page carries the signed-in actions (bookmark, kudos, author tools) - a signed-in reader keeps the application, an anonymous one gets the document. Acceptance per page: a test that fetches the HTML, parses it and asserts the content with no script execution, plus a live probe; the Svelte route is removed in the same commit so the count only goes down. PROGRESS 50635a36: landing page (8a51f9de) and work page /works/{id} shipped as documents, each with a no-script test and a live probe. The work page uses reading_decision_publishing_metadata, answers every denial with one 404 page (bodies compared byte for byte in the test), shows a restricted work's record and withholds its text, and hands a signed-in reader the application per ADR 0006. REMAINING per ADR 0006's order: fandom and tag pages, search results, author page, collection and series pages - each deletes its Svelte route in the same commit. TAG PAGE ed9c7088: GET /tags/{tag} is a document listing the works behind a tag (query filters published public works; empty tag = 404 page; capped at 50 with 'more than 50' rather than a false total). The document shell moved to routes/document.rs at the third caller and work_page's copy was deleted. REMAINING: search results, author page, collection and series pages; then delete the Svelte routes for the pages already served as documents.
